newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index call vols up on rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index call vols up on rally.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. stock index options popped up as the market shot higher in late morning trading, options traders said Tuesday.
"The rally was fast and furious," one S&P 500 index .SPX futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "It put some volatility in the calls.
"The puts are still hanging out, but the calls really picked up," he said.
At about 1140 CDT/1640 GMT, the Dow industrial average .DJI was up 44 points at 7,333 shortly after reaching an intraday high of 7,340.
The SPX was ahead 3.57 at 849.93 and the S&P 100 index gained 4.57 to 831.51. June S&P 500 futures added 6.40 to 852.60.
In the OEX, volatility as measured by the volatility index which is calculated off certain near-month options, was up 0.63, or 2.87 percent, at 22.55, off its 22.91 session high.
Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX, said volatility has been creeping higher recently and could continue to hold firm into Friday's all-important U.S. jobs report for May.

"There's not a supply of calls here, which has been the case," he said. "I think you'll probably see prices appreciate going into Thursday evening, then we'll see if they merit a good move or not come Friday morning."
The employment report is scheduled for release Friday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT, before the stock market opens.

According to a Reuters survey, economists on average expect nonfarm payrolls to rise by 221,000, compared with 142,000 in April. The jobless rate is expected to rise to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent. Average hourly earnings are forecast to climb by 0.4 percent after a 0.1 percent drop in April.
Options traders said activity had slowed down after a flurry of activity off the opening bell.
In the OEX, the heaviest volume was in the June 800 puts, which traded nearly 4,100 contracts. The June 820 put traded about 2,900 and the June 830 put traded 2,145.
Among OEX calls, the June 830 was most active, with turnover of 2,250 contracts. The June 820 calls traded about 2,230 and the June 850 and 860 calls each traded nearly 1,900 contracts.
